study-plan.prompt: Which habits make study stick? (select all)
study-plan.explanation: Active recall and building beat re-reading.
options: Re-deriving a key result from memory each week
Building a checkpoint project at the end of each phase
Writing a short README or post explaining each project
Reading every lesson twice without doing exercises

study-plan.prompt: According to the roadmap, which course should a newcomer to programming start with?
study-plan.explanation: Everything else builds on fluent Python.

study-plan.prompt: Consistency matters more than intensity when following a long study plan.
study-plan.explanation: Regular moderate effort compounds; streaks help build the habit.

interviews.prompt: What does STAR stand for in behavioural interviews?
interviews.explanation: Structure each story this way and quantify the result.

interviews.prompt: In a coding interview, what should you do before writing code?
interviews.explanation: Communication is graded as much as the final code.
options: Restate the problem, ask about constraints and edge cases, and outline a brute-force approach

interviews.prompt: Your training loss isn't decreasing. Which checks come first? (select all)
options: Whether the model can overfit a single small batch
Whether the initial loss is about ln⁡C\ln ClnC
Whether inputs and labels are aligned

interviews.prompt: Why is ROC-AUC potentially misleading on heavily imbalanced data?
interviews.explanation: Use PR curves to see precision directly.
options: The false positive rate divides by a huge number of negatives, so many false alarms still look small
ROC-AUC cannot be computed for imbalanced data

portfolio.prompt: Which project attributes impress hiring managers most? (select all)
portfolio.explanation: Three excellent projects beat thirty tutorials.
options: A real problem with real data
A baseline and an honest evaluation
A deployed demo with a clear write-up

portfolio.explanation: Specific impact with numbers beats lists of tools.
options: "Cut p95 latency 40% by quantizing and batching the ranking model"

portfolio.prompt: Projects in under-served areas (for example Arabic or Darija NLP) can stand out because they are harder to copy.
portfolio.explanation: Differentiation is valuable in a crowded field.

papers.prompt: In the three-pass method, what do you do in the first pass?
papers.explanation: Five minutes is enough to decide whether to go deeper.
options: Read the title, abstract, figures and conclusion to decide relevance

papers.prompt: A paper reports a 0.3-point gain without error bars over three seeds. What should you ask? (select all)
papers.explanation: Small gains are often within noise.
options: Is the gain larger than seed-to-seed variance?
Were the baselines tuned as carefully?
What did the improvement cost in compute?
Nothing; all published results are reliable

papers.prompt: Re-implementing the core idea of a paper in a small notebook is where real understanding happens.
papers.explanation: Implementation exposes every detail the text glosses over.

__exam.prompt: In an ML system design interview, you are asked to design spam detection. What do you do first?
options: Clarify scale, latency, cost of errors and available labels

__exam.prompt: Which statements about the AI engineer interview loop are generally true? (select all)
options: It usually includes coding and ML fundamentals
System design matters more for senior roles

__exam.prompt: What makes a strong answer to "explain a project you are proud of"?
__exam.explanation: Interviewers look for judgement and ownership.
options: The problem, your specific decisions, what failed, and measured results

__exam.prompt: Reading papers is more valuable when you reproduce at least one key result.
__exam.explanation: Reproduction is the best test of understanding.
